speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck pain, arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness; could you please describe exactly where the pain is located and if these symptoms affect specific fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your feet or toes, which might suggest peripheral neuropathy? Also, regarding the motor vehicle accident three years ago, were there any specific neck injuries or fractures documented at that time?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and progressive weakness alongside your sensory symptoms suggests a motor neuron pathology. To confirm this, I need to see if we have results from an MRI of your cervical spine and EMG/Nerve Conduction Studies. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine; REQUEST TEST: EMG_NCS
